jaw.citation: Bourke et al. 2008, PLoS ONE 3(5):e2200, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0002200

jaw.context: distance between upper and lower canine teeth at mouth opening during chewing (EM micro-sensors on canines, 60 Hz). Not an angle: authors note it is not a true gape angle. Not affected by food type (p = 0.47). Motion is a pure hinge, no meaningful side-to-side motion.
jaw.citation: Goldschmidt S, Chew HP, Guy S, Fok A. 2025. Characterizing masticatory motion of dogs using optical and electromagnetic motion tracking. Front Vet Sci 12:1625335. doi 10.3389/fvets.2025.1625335

jaw.context: mean chewing (jaw open-close) frequency over all foods, from FFT of canine-gap signal
food-type means; kibble highest (2.93 Hz); harder treats (>1000 N to fracture) about 2.5 Hz, softer about 2.8 Hz; within-dog SD 0.27 Hz
whole yawn (Barbizet definition), adult dogs; breed means 1.43-2.83 s; longer in breeds with heavier brains
jaw.citation: Gallup AC, Moscatello L, Massen JJM. 2020. Brain weight predicts yawn duration across domesticated dog breeds. Curr Zool 66(4):401-405. doi 10.1093/cz/zoz060
jaw.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (fact only; per-breed table NOT copied)

jaw.context: delay between seeing a yawn and yawning back (behaviour timing, not jaw motion)
jaw.citation: Romero T, Ito M, Saito A, Hasegawa T. 2014. Social modulation of contagious yawning in wolves. PLoS ONE 9(8):e105963

jaw.context: respiratory (panting) rate plateau while walking 12 min in tropical sun; rises from about 47 at rest/cool to 374 breaths/min at black-globe temperature above 35 C
jaw.citation: do Nascimento PV, Saraiva EP, Verissimo TNS et al. 2026. Cool and safe walks: heat stress threshold for domestic dogs living in hot and sunny regions. Int J Biometeorol. doi 10.1007/s00484-026-03236-y

jaw.context: hot walks; the same paper cites Higgins & Iampietro 1967: over 350 breaths/min in heat chambers

NOT FOUND: no open measurement of jaw angle during panting, barking or howling. Fitch 2000 (Phonetica, X-ray video of barking dogs) shows larynx lowering only (abstract; not open). Wolf howling tongue-gesture preprint (Ekstrom et al. 2024, Research Square, CC BY, doi 10.21203/rs.3.rs-5354163/v1) gives no jaw angle in the abstract; full text page is a JS app and could not be read.

NOT FETCHED: Gart et al. 2015 PNAS 112:15798 (dog lapping kinematics, 19 dogs) and Crompton & Musinsky 2011 Biol Lett 7:882 (X-ray lapping; at least 3 lap cycles per swallow) are not in the Europe PMC open-access subset (fullTextXML HTTP 500 x3) and pnas.org returned 403. Only abstract facts recorded: at least three lap cycles are needed to move water to the oesophagus (Crompton & Musinsky 2011).

head_tilt.unit: deg (roll of the outer-eye-corner line, start frame to peak frame)
head_tilt.n: about 132 tilts from 41 of 103 pet dogs
head_tilt.context: owner-filmed 30 s phone videos; tilts mostly when the owner speaks familiar words. Values digitised by me from the paper's Fig. 3 (left panel, y axis 'rotation amplitude (degrees)'), pixel-to-degree by the gridlines (0 and 80 deg); dot count 118-132 depending on overlap handling, matches the expected count (Condition 3 + 4 tilt totals, about 134). Accuracy about +-1.5 deg per dot. Camera perspective inflates/deflates 2-D roll, so the 60-90 deg tail is probably partly measurement artefact.
head_tilt.citation: Buckley C, Sexton CL, Martvel G, Hecht EE, Bradley BJ, Zamansky A, Subiaul F. 2025. What does that head tilt mean? Brain lateralization and sex differences in the processing of familiar human speech by domestic dogs. Animals 15(21):3179. doi 10.3390/ani15213179

head_tilt.context: one example trace (paper Fig. 2): fast rise to peak in about 0.7 s, then a slow sag over about 10 s with a second small tilt at about 14 s. Read by eye from the figure.
owner speaks familiar words (Condition 4). Baseline/eye contact only 0.019; unfamiliar speech 0.184. 40% of dogs tilted at least once.
right preferred at population level (chi2 p = 0.029); each dog keeps its side

head_tilt.unit: share of trials with a tilt
head_tilt.context: when owner names a toy to fetch; side stable across months (r = 0.74-0.84). No angle or duration measured.
head_tilt.citation: Sommese A, Miklosi A, Pogany A, Temesi A, Dror S, Fugazza C. 2022. An exploratory analysis of head-tilting in dogs. Anim Cogn 25:701-705. doi 10.1007/s10071-021-01571-8

ears.context: NOT FOUND. No open study gives dog or wolf pinna rotation angles or movement durations. DogFACS codes ear actions (EAD101 forward, EAD102 adductor, EAD103 flattener, EAD104 rotator, EAD105 downward) as presence/duration of events, not angles. Automated-landmark papers (Martvel & Riemer 2025 Sci Rep, CC BY, PMC12405473; Martvel et al. 2025 BMC Vet Res, CC BY-NC-ND, PMC12102829) excluded pinna landmarks or report classifier results only; Martvel & Riemer found ear-base landmarks (ears drawn back) separate fireworks-fear from control best, without angles.
